decisions.reason: After two years on the market, this automation product has accumulated development effort and public commitment and remains tightly aligned with the firm's digital-control strategy, so management would be inclined to persist unless setbacks became unmistakably structural.

This fouling detection system still fits the firm's push toward smarter monitoring and efficiency in infrastructure operations, and with prior investment and no clear failure signal, disappointing uptake can still be read as temporary.

Although this mechanical weir product is less central to the firm's digital future than its software-heavy launches, it is close to the established water-infrastructure offer and management would usually give a recent launch more time before admitting a misstep.

The energy management system matches the firm's announced direction toward networked, efficient and environmentally beneficial infrastructure, so sunk development effort, strategic centrality and public launch make continued backing likely.

As a visible multi-model product line with its own page, this overflow flap gate reflects a meaningful commercial commitment within the firm's core water-control business, which management is likely to defend unless market rejection becomes clear.
